findings.title: stable + MSRV clippy gates RED at HEAD on install_plugin too_many_lines (103/100) — FP-F4 regression
findings.evidence: `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets --features benten-eval/testing,benten-engine/test-helpers,benten-graph/testing,benten-crypto-suite/testing -- -D warnings` emits: `error: this function has too many lines (103/100)` at `pub fn install_plugin<F, M, P>(...)`. Same error reproduces on `cargo +1.95 clippy ...` with the same feature spec. The function grew past the 100-line clippy threshold from FP-F4's two additions: (a) commit a14692b6 `feat(plugin-trust): consult check_install_consent at install-pipeline step 3c + mint PluginInstallConsentDenied (D-3-a close)` adding ~15 LOC at step 3c, and (b) commit b5a6e758 `fix(platform-foundation): L2-R6-MAJOR-1 — wire T10-upgrade (a) into install_plugin (R6 R1 fix-pass)` adding the T10-upgrade caps-grew check. Net delta crosses the clippy ceiling. The R6 R1 L12 lens at HEAD 4bbc4cac was clean; this is a regression introduced by the FP merge. Per pim-N-stable-clippy-gate (§3.5j) this gate IS mandatory pre-merge — and per §3.5h MANDATORY-PRE-MERGE the orchestrator workspace pre-push verification clause was bypassed (mini-review APPROVE didn't substitute). Pim-N-cite-drift-fp1-recurrence is the directly-applicable codification.
findings.destination: R6 R2 fix-pass (this branch or sibling FP cycle): EITHER (a) refactor install_plugin: extract the cap-policy step (steps 3c + 3d cap-grew check) into a separate `fn check_install_caps<F, M, P>(...)` helper that returns `Result<(), ErrorCode>` (cleanest; restores readability), OR (b) add `#[allow(clippy::too_many_lines, reason = "install pipeline is a sequenced step list — splitting fragments the invariant ordering documented in docs/PLUGIN-MANIFEST.md §4.1")]` directly on the function (consistent with the existing as_static_str + as_str + routed_edge_label allow-with-reason pattern in benten-errors). Decision between (a) and (b) belongs to the FP-F4 author for context; either is correct. The §3.5h orchestrator pre-push workspace clippy gate MUST run BEFORE the FP merge, not after (the existing §3.5h amendment in pim-cite-drift-fp1-recurrence is the locking rule; failure here is process-discipline-not-followed, not new rule needed).

findings.title: §3.5j feature-spec is stale post-FP-A F1ab — missing benten-crypto-suite/testing breaks 7 crypto-suite test compiles under both stable + MSRV clippy
findings.where: Standing spec at .addl/dispatch-conventions.md §3.5j + every CI clippy invocation using the historical 3-crate feature-list (e.g. .github/workflows/ci.yml + .github/workflows/cargo-public-api.yml + .github/workflows/phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml). Affected test files: crates/benten-crypto-suite/tests/{tf2_no_hardcoded_sizes_ml_dsa65_vector, tf3a_pq_hybrid_wasm32_roundtrip, tf3a_structural_kdf_step_root_derivation, tf3a_x_wing_hybrid_wrap_x25519_mlkem768_codepoint_0x647a, tf4_gcore3c_swap_matrix_conformance_additional, canonical_bytes_v1_codepoints_and_aad}.rs
findings.evidence: FP-A bundle F1ab commit e17ccadf (`chore(phase-4-meta-core-r6r1-fp-a-F1ab): workspace _for_test cfg-gating sweep + testing feature additions`) added `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testing"))]` to multiple `pub fn .*_for_test*` constructors in crates/benten-crypto-suite (including `SwapMatrix::generate_keypair_for_test` at swap_matrix.rs:355, `SwapMatrix::generate_recipient_keypair_for_test` at :377, `CipherSuite::generate_recipient_keypair_for_test`, `HybridSignature::flip_pq_byte_for_test`, `HybridSignature::without_pq_half_for_test`, `StructuralKdfKey::derive_step_without_info_tag_for_test`, `SizeTouchingSurfaces::redb_store_for_test`, `UcanVarsigV1Header::with_raw_codepoint_for_test`). The crate's `[features] testing = []` declaration was added at the same time. Integration tests under `tests/` are SEPARATE compilation units that do NOT inherit `cfg(test)` from the crate-under-test; they need the `testing` feature explicitly. The standing §3.5j spec at dispatch-conventions.md line ~378 names the feature list as `--features benten-eval/testing,benten-engine/test-helpers,benten-graph/testing` (3 crates only) — extending the cfg-gate to crypto-suite broke that spec atomically without the spec sweep. CI verification: 16 E0599 errors when running stable clippy with the historical 3-crate spec; 0 errors when adding `benten-crypto-suite/testing`. This is the same pattern as fix-up #13 (Gate 6 bench compile needed `--features benten-engine/test-helpers` post-A's F2 rename) — the FP-A cfg-gate sweep added the feature gate without sweeping every downstream invocation site.
findings.destination: R6 R2 fix-pass (this branch or sibling FP cycle): (1) update .addl/dispatch-conventions.md §3.5j feature list from `--features benten-eval/testing,benten-engine/test-helpers,benten-graph/testing` to `--features benten-eval/testing,benten-engine/test-helpers,benten-graph/testing,benten-crypto-suite/testing` (one-line edit; also extend §3.5g item 6 'cross-tool config mirror' to name the 4 crates instead of 3). (2) sweep every CI workflow invoking workspace clippy or `cargo build --tests` with the historical 3-crate spec — extend to the 4-crate spec. Audit shell: `grep -rln 'benten-eval/testing,benten-engine/test-helpers,benten-graph/testing' .github/workflows/ scripts/` to enumerate; expected affected workflows include cargo-public-api.yml + phase-2a-exit-criteria.yml + ci.yml + any other clippy-running surface. Pim-N candidate: 'cfg-gate addition cascades to feature-spec mirror at EVERY clippy/test-compile invocation' (extends §3.5g item #4 cross-tool config mirror to cover feature-spec-mirror-across-CI-invocations). Pairs with the fix-up #13 datapoint that bench files were also missed.

findings.title: Rustdoc broken-link drift — 3 stale `Engine::get_node` cites in engine_wait.rs should be `Engine::read_node` per G-CORE-9 row D-4/D-22 rename
findings.where: crates/benten-engine/src/engine_wait.rs:1134, 1142, 1145 (3 source locations; 5 rustdoc-warning instances — line 1145 cites 'whose principal is root by construction' + line 1142 cites in 'are not a checked vs bypass pair', so a single source line generates 2 warnings via 2 paragraphs)
findings.evidence: Running `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D missing_docs' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --features testing` emits 5 `warning: unresolved link to \`Engine::get_node\`` lines pointing at engine_wait.rs:1134:48, :1142:41, :1145:43. `grep -rn 'pub fn get_node' crates/benten-engine/src/` returns ONLY hits under `testing.rs:1109 pub fn get_node` (which is the cfg-gated test-helper re-export) — the canonical `Engine::get_node` was renamed to `Engine::read_node` per G-CORE-9 V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE row D-4 (refer §1.A.FROZEN). The doc comment paragraphs at engine_wait.rs:1134-1150 are the `pub fn read_node_as` docstring that explicitly differentiates against `Engine::read_node` (the un-attributed engine-internal read path) — the rename pass missed these intra-doc cites. Not gated by `-D missing_docs` (which only fires on undocumented `pub` items, not on broken links), so these slipped past the missing-docs workspace test. The `cargo doc` invocation itself does NOT use `-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links` flag (which would promote these to errors). The §3.5j stable+MSRV clippy gate also doesn't promote rustdoc lints. Same class as r6-r1-l12 OBS-1 (feature-flag coverage) but actively manifesting at HEAD rather than coverage-gap.
findings.destination: R6 R2 fix-pass — orchestrator-direct (3-line edit): replace 3 occurrences of `[\`Engine::get_node\`]` with `[\`Engine::read_node\`]` at engine_wait.rs:1134, 1142, 1145. Pairs with a §3.5j amendment to add `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links'` to the workspace doc gate (or alternatively add `--cap-lints warn` flag inversion). Pim-N candidate: 'public-method rename cascade must include intra-doc-link sweep' (the existing pim-N-cross-language-rule-mirror §3.5g doesn't currently name intra-doc-cite mirrors as a 'config-mirror' surface; this is a 4th-recurrence-class candidate — earlier recurrences: TauriRender vs TauriRenderer 8-cite drift R6 R1 L12 #3 extension; cargo-audit ↔ deny.toml R6 R2 methodology #4 extension; bench-files-vs-test-files fix-up #13).
